note: python tools/research/phase7_extension/p2_audit.py --results research/phase7/results         --out research/phase7_extension/results/p2_statistical_audit.json  Recomputed from the committed per-object outputs only (confirmation_orders.json, confirmation_trials.json.gz):  1. the paired table of robustness (v3, six standard conditions, torsion 0.005) of Joint vs M0; 2. the pre-specified test (paired-difference z test with the sample SD, ddof 1; margin -5 pp) and its Holm step; 3. alternatives for paired binary data, as sensitivity analyses:    - Wald test with the multinomial (MLE) variance of the paired difference;    - Tango's score test for a paired difference (Tango 1998, Statistics in Medicine 17:891-908) at the margin,      and the score interval obtained by inverting it;    - Newcombe's hybrid score interval for a paired difference (Newcombe 1998, Statistics in Medicine      17:2635-2650, method 10), without continuity correction; 4. the full-precision one-sided p-values of the whole primary family and Holm recomputed with them; 5. fragility: the pre-specified test after changing the Joint outcome of a single object.  The references above are cited for the formulas; they are not yet in references_verified.json.

pre_specified.method: pre-specified: z test, sample SD of the paired differences (ddof 1)

tango.method: Tango score test at the margin, and its inverted 95 % interval

newcombe_method10.method: Newcombe hybrid score interval (method 10), no continuity correction

conclusion: The pre-specified test supports non-inferiority narrowly (lower bound -4.9 pp vs margin -5). Score-based methods for paired binary data do not: see tango and newcombe_method10. The pre-specified result is kept as the confirmatory result; the discrepancy is reported.
